title: The practices, looking back
hookLine: prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting, song
tomorrow: why would a gospel end with people too scared to talk?

lines: PRAYER, REST, A PAGE, A GIFT, A FAST, A SONG.
cards: A gym membership, a language-app streak, a journal with three pages filled in: good starts pile up. This path has offered six old practices: prayer, a day of rest, scripture, giving, fasting, song.
Some found room in an ordinary week and kept it. Some lasted a few days and slipped away. Both tell you something.

teach.b: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus talks about giving, prayer and fasting in a row, and the grammar is the thing to tell a friend: he says when, not if.
“But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.” “But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet.”
And a fast that doesn't show: “But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face.”
Each one done quietly, each one assumed, part of an ordinary week rather than a trophy.

The sabbath gets the same gentleness in Mark: “The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.” A practice serves the person, not the other way round, so it can bend when a life changes shape.
And Paul gives scripture and song one line: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.” Dwell means live there. Move in.
Unpack. That may be the real test of a practice: not how hard it was tried in the first week, but whether it moved in.
Looking back, the one that stayed may simply be the one that fit.

how: Christians keep these practices in many forms: daily prayer, a day of rest, Bible reading, giving, seasons of fasting such as Lent, and singing in worship and at home.

o: habits of faith that move in and stay
a test of how hard you tried this year
rules you must keep to earn God's love

p: let not thy left hand know
for man, not man for it

s: Jesus says 'when thou prayest', not 'if thou prayest'
in Matthew 6 he speaks of giving, prayer and fasting as things that will happen.
a practice that slips was never real
the sabbath was made for man: a practice serves the person, and can be reshaped.
in Mark, the parables' meaning went to whoever came back and asked
when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.

games.q: your morning prayer habit fell apart when your job moved to early shifts. a friend says that proves it was never real. which line fits best?
o: reshape it to fit the new hours; the sabbath was made for man.
double it from now on, as a penalty for slipping.
drop it; if it were meant for you, it wouldn't have slipped.
games.why: the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: a practice serves the person, so it can bend when a life changes shape.

practice: Count the six on your fingers, slowly: prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting, song. At each one, notice whether it still lives in your week, even in a small form, and fold a finger down for each that stayed.
Then rest with the one that stayed longest; if you pray, give thanks for it.

wordCard.voice: The practices. Prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting and song: not achievements, but habits that move in and stay.

orig.note: the Greek for 'let dwell' in Colossians 3:16: let the word move in.

carryVoice: Keep this: what stayed, or in Paul's word, what dwells in you. A week from the top, done.
